rs232.pinout: pin 2 = transmit from the dCS unit, pin 3 = receive into the dCS unit, pin 5 = ground; wired straight through, pin 1 to pin 1
rs232.note: Two serial modes, chosen in Settings → RS232: B = Binary (dCS's own production protocol) and T = Text (the ASCII commands recorded here). Text mode must be selected before any of these strings will be accepted, and on Vivaldi it needs firmware 1.20 or later. BAUD RATE IS SETTLED, and not by the published documents: dCS confirmed directly (2026-09-23) that Vivaldi runs Text mode at 4800 baud, the same as Binary, while Rossini and Bartók run Text mode at 115200. The Rossini manual's "Text is 115200" is therefore correct FOR ROSSINI and does not describe Vivaldi — which is what made the two documents look contradictory. Use 4800 here and do not try 115200 as a fallback. Lina has no serial port at all, so no dCS text-mode entry can exist for it.

ir.note: Philips RC-5 on a 37.9 kHz carrier. dCS assign one RC-5 category per function group rather than per box, so 0x0D addresses DAC functions wherever they live — the same address drives the DAC section of a Puccini Player. dCS advise sending every command three times, because a single burst is not reliably decoded.

controls.label: Wake from sleep
controls.note: Wakes a sleeping unit. There is no command that powers up a unit switched off at the rear, because the serial interface is unpowered in that state.
Only acted on if the unit is already asleep — send SLEEP 1 first and allow it to settle. Sent to an awake unit it does nothing, which reads as a dead serial link.

params.name: level
params.note: Absolute attenuation, 0 dB being full output. Substitute for n.

params.name: delta
params.note: Signed offset from the present setting. A negative value attenuates, so this one command covers both directions — it is filed under volume_up only because the vocabulary has no signed-adjust action.

params.name: input
params.note: Substitute the number for n. This enumeration is specific to the Vivaldi DAC's input complement; the other dCS DACs number their own inputs differently and must not inherit it.

controls.note: Returns a status report, so unlike most gear here this device is readable rather than write-only — but the reply's exact layout is not published, which is why no reply pattern is recorded. HELP lists the commands the connected unit accepts, which is the quickest way to establish what a given firmware supports.
Same restriction as the serial equivalent: it only takes effect if the unit is already in Sleep.

metadata.notes: The reason this device is in the registry: the Vivaldi DAC has no Ethernet of its own, so RS-232 and infrared are the only ways to control it. In a full Vivaldi stack the Upsampler provides the network connection, and the DAC still has to be driven separately over serial or IR. Its own volume control is genuinely useful, which makes it a plausible preamplifier replacement and therefore worth automating. Command encodings come from dCS's Remote Control Codes document, which carries an explicit note that the codes are for controlling dCS equipment from third-party control systems — they are manufacturer-published facts, and the attribution above should travel with them. Baud provenance: the Remote Control Codes document and the Rossini manual disagreed on Text-mode baud, and this entry previously recorded the value as unresolved with "try 4800, then 115200". dCS resolved it directly on 2026-09-23: the rate is per range, not per mode — Vivaldi 4800, Rossini and Bartók 115200, and Lina has no serial port for dCS control. Only that datum came from the manufacturer, so contributedBy is deliberately absent: the rest of the entry is still read off published documents.
